scope: Three proposed M280 occurrences flagged by the parent. Independent image/inventory comparison; primary table frequency is not the decision criterion.

records.recommendation: Recommend replacing M280 with M283; retain leading UNKNOWN from supplied line, which is outside this targeted audit.
reasons: The final diamond has a separate small enclosed cell at its right boundary, absent from M280.
Its internal stroke runs obliquely down-left rather than forming the small symmetric fork of M280. Numbered M283 combines this oblique internally marked stem with an extra right-hand cell.
M279 also has an extra right cell, but its interior has two curved descending legs; that morphology is less consistent with the angular oblique stem visible here. M277 lacks the extra right cell.
The scan blurs the tiny terminal ticks, so rejection of M280 is firmer than the detailed M283 identification. No total-frequency target was used to select the sign.
records.confidence: High rejection of M280; moderate-to-high M283 identification because fine internal ticks are blurred.

additional_crop.generation: Primary PDF594 rendered with pdftoppm -scale-to4200; crop rounded coordinates derived from [1010,120,1260,220] at2600px page height, then resized1000x400. Source PDF hash recorded at top level.

reasons: The diamond has a small top cell with a descending central stem that branches into a short fork; it matches numbered M280.
No extra enclosed right-edge cell or long oblique stem is visible. M277 lacks the lower fork; M279/M283 introduce an additional right cell.
Full Texts page authenticates reference4468 with first-line metadata310001. The second glyph is a diamond with a top cell and a short branched central stem.
The high-resolution crop supports the internal fork of M280, not the simple unbranched stem of M277 or the extra right-edge cell of M279/M283.

conclusion: The two clear M280 occurrences are5325/20 and4468/10. The final sign of3234/10 differs visibly and is best matched to M283, with a fine-detail scan-quality qualification. This explains the apparent excess independently of a forced frequency fit.
limitations: The opening UNKNOWN of3234/10 was not assigned an identity in this bounded audit.
Glyph identities concern Mahadevan editorial drawings, not independent artifact photographs.
